introduction.definition: A chimney or stack releases flue gases high above the ground so they disperse safely. Hot gas rises by natural draft. Steel stacks are lined against heat and acid condensation, fitted with helical strakes against wind vibration, and carry sampling ports, platforms and warning lights.

introduction.summary: A chimney (stack) discharges flue gases high enough to disperse them safely. Hot gas rises by natural draft; height and exit velocity set the dispersion. Steel stacks are lined against acid condensation, fitted with helical strakes against wind-induced vibration, and carry sampling ports, platforms and an aviation light.

video_tutorials.title: Chimney / Stack — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Chimney / Stack.
A chimney or stack releases flue gases high above the ground so they disperse safely.
Hot gas rises by natural draft.
Steel stacks are lined against heat and acid condensation, fitted with helical strakes against wind vibration, and carry sampling ports, platforms and warning lights.
Typical applications include boilers and furnaces; power plants and incinerators; process heaters and gas turbines; kilns and dryers.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Chimney / Stack — Operation

script.narration: How the Chimney / Stack works.
Flue gas enters through the breeching.
It rises up the lined shell by draft.
Strakes break up wind vortices.
Gas is sampled at the ports for emissions monitoring.
The plume disperses above the top.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Chimney / Stack — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Chimney / Stack.
Check lights and CEMS.
Inspect shell thickness and lining.
Repaint/re-line; inspect anchor bolts.
Watch for acid corrosion: thinning, holes. Common cause: flue gas below dew point.
Watch for wind vibration: oscillation. Common cause: vortex shedding.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
